about: The instance variables of the former Horos and OsiriX plugin SDK that a class now implemented in Swift keeps as stored fields, each with the linker alias that exports the field's offset under the name a plugin's binary looks up, _OBJC_IVAR_$_Class.ivar. A plugin built for either SDK reads and writes these variables directly, from a subclass or from a category of the host's class, and its binary binds every such name when it loads: one that is missing refuses the whole bundle.

Horos/Scripts/Horos/legacy-plugin-ivar-aliases.rsp, the linker response file of the application target, is the rendering of this table: for each entry of ivars, in the order they have here, a line '-alias <symbol> _OBJC_IVAR_$_<Class.ivar>' and a line '-u _OBJC_IVAR_$_<Class.ivar>', which keeps the name through dead stripping. The response file takes no comments; what there is to say is said here. tests/test-legacy-plugin-instance-variables.py fails when the file is not this rendering, and writes it with --write-aliases.

An entry is named 'Class.ivar': the class by its Objective-C runtime name and the variable as the SDK's header declared it. sdk is the C type of that declaration (an array as 'unsigned char[256]'). field is the Swift stored field that holds it. symbol is that field's offset symbol, as nm lists it in the objects of a build; xcrun swift-demangle shows it as 'direct field offset for <Module>.<Class>.<field> : <Type>'. state is live (the application reads and writes the field), derived (the application keeps the field up to date where the SDK's code wrote it, and does not read it) or inert (nothing of the application stands behind it: the field has the exact type and stays 0, NO or nil unless a plugin writes it). ownership is value (not an object), strong (the class releases it when it goes), unowned (stored with no retain and never released) or manual (retained by its setter and never released by the class), as the SDK's own code owned it: a plugin writes the pointer with the retain count that code expected.

Thirty-nine entries of DCMView are declared only by the header of an older SDK of OsiriX, of which plugins carry copies in their sources and with which some were built: curDCM, which that SDK named without the underscore the later one gave it and which the view keeps as a second field with the same image, derived, and thirty-eight that are inert, of the offset of the origin, the lens, the second OpenGL context, the iChat theatre, the reference lines of the former MPR and the view's own copies of the hot keys, the locale and the dates.

The field is a stored 'final var' declared in the class itself (or in its @objc @implementation extension) with the type the C declaration has in memory. It is internal: a private or fileprivate field's symbol is local to its object file, with a hash of the file's name in it, and no alias reaches it, which also holds for the storage a property wrapper synthesizes; a wrapper's struct is therefore declared as a field of its own. It is not let, lazy, weak, computed or observed, and is not inside another struct or object: an offset is relative to the instance. A direct write by a plugin calls no setter and no observer. Renaming a field, changing its type or moving it out of the class changes or removes its symbol, and the application no longer links until the entry follows.
No two entries name the same symbol, and none is given an offset that is not a field of its class.
